headline: Inside game only: Cruz backside Saturday, flats Sunday
body:
Small-craft advisories are up through late Wednesday night in the outer waters, and Saturday's outer-water forecast is worse, not better: NW 25 to 30 knots with 8 to 10 ft seas from Point Sal to Santa Cruz, 6 to 9 ft around San Nicolas. The east Channel stays workable — Harbor winds 5 knots or less with 3.2 to 3.5 ft seas both days, though the western channel blows NW 20 to 30 on Saturday.

Skip the long runs. Santa Rosa Flats shows 24 to 26 knots and 7 to 8 ft seas with water at 62 degrees, well under the bluefin break; San Nicolas at 73 miles and Osborn at 68 aren't worth 5 to 6-plus ft seas for a small boat.

Saturday, run the backside of Santa Cruz for yellowtail: 9 to 11 knots through midday, 3.8 ft, 70.9 degrees — troll the 80-ft line early and be headed home before the 15-knot afternoon breeze. Sunday, seas build there to 4.8 ft, so fish halibut on the Goleta–Carpinteria sand in near-glass conditions.
